> Status: draft. Match the genome build across peaks, fragments, annotations, and sequence resources.

Input: a peak-by-cell count matrix, cell metadata, fragment file, and gene
annotation. The cells run fragment-aware QC, LSI, peak testing, and motif
enrichment; chromVAR is optional.

## 1. Create the Signac object

The count matrix has peaks in rows and cells in columns. Metadata has one row
per cell and contains `cell_id` and `sample_id`.

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(Signac)
library(qs2)
library(readr)

counts <- qs2::qs_read("input/peak_counts.qs2")
metadata <- readr::read_tsv("input/cell_metadata.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
annotation <- qs2::qs_read("input/gene_annotation.qs2")
fragments_path <- "input/fragments.tsv.gz"
stopifnot("cell_id" %in% names(metadata), "sample_id" %in% names(metadata))
stopifnot(!anyNA(metadata$cell_id), !anyDuplicated(metadata$cell_id))
stopifnot(file.exists(fragments_path), file.exists(paste0(fragments_path, ".tbi")))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rownames(counts)), !anyDuplicated(colnames(counts)))

cell_alignment <- data.frame(
  cell_id = c(setdiff(colnames(counts), metadata$cell_id),
              setdiff(metadata$cell_id, colnames(counts))),
  source = c(rep("count_matrix_only", length(setdiff(colnames(counts), metadata$cell_id))),
             rep("metadata_only", length(setdiff(metadata$cell_id, colnames(counts)))))
)
cells <- intersect(colnames(counts), metadata$cell_id)
counts <- counts[, cells, drop = FALSE]
metadata <- metadata[match(cells, metadata$cell_id), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$cell_id

fragment_object <- Signac::CreateFragmentObject(
  path = fragments_path, cells = cells, validate.fragments = TRUE
)
chromatin_assay <- Signac::CreateChromatinAssay(
  counts = counts, sep = c(":", "-"), genome = "hg38",
  annotation = annotation, fragments = fragment_object,
  min.cells = 1, min.features = 1
)
object <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = chromatin_assay,
                                     assay = "ATAC", meta.data = metadata)
DefaultAssay(object) <- "ATAC"
print(object)
```

Change `hg38` and the peak separator to match the input. Fragment files must
be indexed and contain the retained cell barcodes.

## 2. Add fragment-aware QC and filter

`metrics.tsv` has `cell_id`, `passed_filters`, `peak_region_fragments`, and
`blacklist_region_fragments`. These example thresholds are not universal.

```{r}
metrics <- readr::read_tsv("input/singlecell_metrics.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(metrics$cell_id))
metrics <- metrics[match(colnames(object), metrics$cell_id), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(metrics$cell_id, colnames(object)))
metrics$pct_reads_in_peaks <- 100 * metrics$peak_region_fragments / metrics$passed_filters
metrics$blacklist_ratio <- metrics$blacklist_region_fragments / metrics$peak_region_fragments
rownames(metrics) <- metrics$cell_id
object <- Seurat::AddMetaData(object, metrics[, setdiff(names(metrics), "cell_id"), drop = FALSE])
object <- Signac::NucleosomeSignal(object)
object <- Signac::TSSEnrichment(object, fast = TRUE)

qc_metadata <- object[[]]
object$qc_pass <- with(qc_metadata,
  is.finite(nCount_ATAC) & is.finite(passed_filters) &
    is.finite(pct_reads_in_peaks) & is.finite(blacklist_ratio) &
    is.finite(nucleosome_signal) & is.finite(TSS.enrichment) &
    nCount_ATAC >= 1000 & passed_filters >= 3000 &
    pct_reads_in_peaks >= 25 & blacklist_ratio <= 0.05 &
    nucleosome_signal <= 1.5 & TSS.enrichment >= 6
)
print(table(object$sample_id, object$qc_pass, useNA = "ifany"))
VlnPlot(object, features = c("nCount_ATAC", "nFeature_ATAC",
                             "nucleosome_signal", "TSS.enrichment"),
        group.by = "sample_id", ncol = 2, pt.size = 0)
object <- subset(object, subset = qc_pass)
```

Inspect missing values and distributions before filtering. Retain the
per-sample counts so the filter cannot hide a library-specific failure.

## 3. Run TF-IDF, LSI, clustering, and UMAP

```{r}
object <- Signac::RunTFIDF(object)
object <- Signac::FindTopFeatures(object, min.cutoff = "q5")
object <- Signac::RunSVD(object, n = 50)
Signac::DepthCor(object, reduction = "lsi")

# Inspect DepthCor before deciding whether to include LSI1.
object <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(object, reduction = "lsi", dims = 2:30,
                                graph.name = c("atac_nn", "atac_snn"))
object <- Seurat::FindClusters(object, graph.name = "atac_snn",
                               resolution = 0.5, random.seed = 1)
object <- Seurat::RunUMAP(object, reduction = "lsi", dims = 2:30,
                          reduction.name = "umap_atac", seed.use = 1)
DimPlot(object, reduction = "umap_atac", group.by = "seurat_clusters", label = TRUE)
```

LSI is a representation of accessibility. It does not correct batch effects.

## 4. Find differential peaks and motif enrichment

The example compares two clusters. The background is all peaks in the assay;
change it only when the study has a justified background universe.

```{r}
library(JASPAR2024)
library(TFBSTools)
library(RSQLite)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)

Seurat::Idents(object) <- "seurat_clusters"
peak_results <- Seurat::FindMarkers(object, ident.1 = "0", ident.2 = "1",
                                    assay = "ATAC", test.use = "LR",
                                    latent.vars = "nCount_ATAC")
foreground <- rownames(peak_results)[peak_results$p_val_adj < 0.05]
background <- rownames(object[["ATAC"]])
stopifnot(length(foreground) > 0)

database <- JASPAR2024::JASPAR2024()
connection <- RSQLite::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), JASPAR2024::db(database))
motifs <- TFBSTools::getMatrixSet(connection, opts = list(
  collection = "CORE", tax_group = "vertebrates", species = 9606,
  all_versions = FALSE
))
RSQLite::dbDisconnect(connection)

object <- Signac::AddMotifs(object, genome = BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38,
                            pfm = motifs, assay = "ATAC")
motif_results <- Signac::FindMotifs(object, features = foreground,
                                    background = background, assay = "ATAC")
head(motif_results[order(motif_results$p.adjust), ], 20)
```

Peak-level tests are exploratory when individual cells are treated as
replicates. Use a sample-aware method for population-level claims.

## 5. Estimate cell-level motif deviations with chromVAR (optional)

Motif enrichment and chromVAR answer different questions. The first tests a
peak set; chromVAR estimates bias-corrected deviations per cell.

```{r}
#| eval: false

library(chromVAR)
peak_counts <- Seurat::GetAssayData(object, assay = "ATAC", layer = "counts")
motif_annotations <- Signac::GetMotifData(object, assay = "ATAC", slot = "data")
deviations <- chromVAR::computeDeviations(
  object = peak_counts,
  annotations = t(motif_annotations)
)
motif_deviations <- chromVAR::deviationScores(deviations)
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_tsv(data.frame(motif = rownames(motif_deviations), motif_deviations),
                 "output/chromvar_deviations.tsv")
```

## 6. Save the object and peak results

```{r}
dir.create("output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
qs2::qs_save(object, "output/scatac_analysis.qs2")
readr::write_tsv(data.frame(peak = rownames(peak_results), peak_results),
                 "output/differential_peaks.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(data.frame(motif = rownames(motif_results), motif_results),
                 "output/motif_enrichment.tsv")
readr::write_tsv(cell_alignment, "output/cell_alignment.tsv")
```
